objective:
Objective: build an entry.c for the conjectures.io "Exact integer kernels" competition (Bittensor subnet 66) that beats the current champion by at least 3% on at least one board, verified locally. Do NOT register a hotkey, do NOT submit, do NOT spend any TAO.

Rules: https://github.com/conjectures-io/exact-integer-kernels-miner/blob/main/RULES.md (read fully first). One C11 file defining eik_sigmoid, eik_tanh, eik_exp on binary32 bit patterns, correctly rounded (nearest, ties to even) on all 2^32 inputs incl. special values; integer arithmetic only (no float types/literals/casts), no #include, no state between calls, no long or plain char, max 256 KiB. Score S = mean instructions per call in an emulator on RV32IM and Cortex-M0+ (thumbv6m), weighted inputs (typical 55%, wide 30%, near-midpoint hard 10%, random 5%) plus a tail term and a code-size term. Lower is better. A candidate needs S <= 0.970x of the champion re-measured on the same inputs, then must pass every input under UBSan/ASan and on target object code. Copies (same preprocessed source after renaming) are rejected.

Step 1 - setup: clone https://github.com/conjectures-io/exact-integer-kernels-miner on Linux x86-64, Python 3.12, gcc; run python -m eik setup. Read current champions and S per board from GET https://conjectures.io/v1/competitions/exact-integer-kernels/boards.
Step 2 - baseline: download the public sources of former champions (https://conjectures.io/v1/competitions/exact-integer-kernels/submissions/<id>/source for ids 50, 48, 46, 42, 37...). Score each locally with eik evaluate; pick the best base per board. Write down which techniques each uses (tables, polynomial degree, range reduction, fast paths, per-target #ifdef).
Step 3 - optimise: find genuine improvements, one technique per experiment, measured with eik evaluate on fresh seeds: cheaper range reduction, smaller/denser tables, better fast paths for the typical and wide input classes, fewer branches, per-target paths (Cortex-M0+ has no 32x32->64 multiply; RV32IM has MULH), lower code size, cheaper handling of hard near-midpoint cases. Keep a log of every experiment with S per board.
Step 4 - verify: for the best candidate run eik check, eik evaluate on several seeds, and eik fullcheck for all three functions (every input, UBSan and ASan) plus the target object-code checks the kit supports. Zero wrong outputs.

Deliverable: entry.c, a table of S per board for the candidate vs the current champion re-measured (ratio), which boards it would take, full check logs, the experiment log, and a short note on what changed versus the base it started from. If no candidate reaches 0.970x, deliver the best entry, its ratios and what to try next.
